meta.summary: CORRECTION of E22-E24: the tertiary cascade does NOT break chemistry — it IMPROVES it. The E22 'crash' was a normalization bug (n_therm=10000 instead of 4096 in every run_irt invocation this session, under-normalizing all G-values by 4096/10000=0.41x). E23/E24's 'over-recombination' investigation chased a phantom.

the_bug: run_irt.cjs signature is <dump> <n_therm> <E_eV>. All session comparisons ran `run_irt <dump> 10000`, passing n_therm=10000 (should be 4096). This scaled every G-value by 0.41x. The E10r production reference (1.56) was correctly normalized, so comparing wrongly-normalized tertiary (0.66) to it created a false 'crash'. Caught by verify-before-asserting when the s=1.0 unscaled production baseline gave 0.640 instead of the expected 1.56.

result_correct_normalization.note: n_therm=4096, both dumps, 1us G-values vs chem6

verdict: The tertiary cascade (E21/E22 implementation) is a CLEAN WIN on BOTH axes: cascade ions 0.766x->0.931x AND chemistry RMS 19.7%->7.6% (every species improved; H2 0.74x->0.99x and H2O2 0.69x->0.93x close the long-standing chem6 1us gap). Primary track unchanged (195.4, bit-exact), E conserved (99.9%). Only H overshoots slightly (0.92x->1.09x). This is the follow-reality fix: tracking the full electron cascade brings the model much closer to Geant4 across the board. MERGE CANDIDATE pending standard revalidation (SSB E13, full energy sweep).
lesson: verify-before-asserting rescued a real result. A units bug in MY invocation made a working fix look broken, and I then chased a non-existent over-recombination through E23-E24. The principle (when a baseline looks wrong, check the harness) caught it. E22-E24 'chemistry breaks / over-recombination' conclusions are RETRACTED.
